subject: get() does not work for input$Name ?

messages.author: bf524a8c0f86fec6
messages.subject: get() does not work for input$Name ?
parts:
Hi Guys,

I would like to access the input$ elements with get(), but somehow they dont see to be compatible?
-     In General get() works with lists - I double check it in the code - see first part
-     input$summary1 exists   - see second part
-     but I cant access it via texxt = get("summary1", input)

My final goal is to access it via
summ1 = paste("summary", 1, sep = "")
texxt = get(summ1, input)

Does anybody have suggestions
Thank you for your help!


################## server.r -  code ##################
shinyServer(
  function(input, output) {

    # In General get() works with lists
    input2 = data.frame(1)
    names(input2) = c("summary2")
    input2$summary2 = TRUE
    texxt = get("summary2", input2)
    typeof(input2)
   
    output$map <- renderPlot({
      # input$summary1 exists           
      if(input$summary1){
        # but I can not access it via get(), even though input is a list as well,
        # see typeof(input) in the plot-caption (if u comment the next line)        
        texxt = get("summary1", input)
        plot(1,1, main = typeof(input))       
      }
    })
   
  }
)

################## ui.r -  code ##################
shinyUI(fluidPage(

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      checkboxInput("summary1", "Summary Statistics", value = FALSE)
    ),
   
    mainPanel(plotOutput("map"))
  )
))

messages.subject: Re: get() does not work for input$Name ?
parts:
It won't work, because input isn't a list, even though it shares some surface similarities. Instead, you can do input[["summary1"]].

-Winston

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: get() does not work for input$Name ?
parts:
I should amend what I said earlier: The `input` object is technically a list (which is why typeof() reports it as such), but it is not a simple list. It also has a class attribute with the value "reactivevalues", and in general it won't behave like a regular list.

-Winston
On Tue, Jan 27, 2015 at 8:01 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:

typeof() is less helpful than class() in this instance (and also in general). class() shows you that this is a "reactivevalues" object, not a regular list.
